An expert review of the build process and error log has been completed.

### Error Identification

The build is failing during the compilation of the MFEM library, a dependency for Laghos. The specific error is:
```
get_hypre_version.cpp:12:10: fatal error: HYPRE_config.h: No such file or directory
```
This occurs because the MFEM build system is attempting to compile a helper utility to detect the version of the HYPRE library. This process requires the `HYPRE_config.h` header file, which is not included in the `libhypre-dev` package provided by Ubuntu 22.04.

### Root Cause Analysis

The Dockerfile attempts to work around this issue by providing the `HYPRE_VERSION=22300` variable to the `make` command. This variable is intended to bypass the version detection step entirely. However, the build still attempts to compile the helper utility, indicating that the `HYPRE_VERSION` variable is not being respected by the build script in this context.

The root cause is that the MFEM makefile, when the `HYPRE_DIR` variable is not set, defaults to assuming that HYPRE is located in a sibling source directory (e.g., `../hypre`). This "local source" mode causes it to ignore the `HYPRE_VERSION` override and attempt to build the version detection utility using incorrect paths, which ultimately fails.

### Recommended Solution

To resolve this, you must explicitly inform the MFEM build system that you are using a system-installed version of HYPRE. This is done by setting the `HYPRE_DIR` variable to the system's prefix, which is `/usr`. This change ensures the build system uses the correct paths for headers and libraries and correctly respects the `HYPRE_VERSION` variable to bypass the problematic auto-detection step.

The redundant `HYPRE_INCLUDE` and `HYPRE_LIBS` variables can be removed, as setting `HYPRE_DIR` allows the makefile to correctly infer these paths.

Here is the corrected Dockerfile:

```dockerfile
# Base image: Ubuntu 22.04 LTS for a stable, modern environment
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Set non-interactive frontend for package installations
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Install dependencies for building Laghos and its dependencies (MFEM, MPI)
# Includes build tools, compilers, Git, MPI libraries, and other required scientific libraries.
# Also includes OpenSSH for MPI communication across nodes and ca-certificates for network access.
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y \
    build-essential \
    g++ \
    gfortran \
    make \
    git \
    ca-certificates \
    libopenmpi-dev \
    openmpi-bin \
    openssh-client \
    openssh-server \
    libmetis-dev \
    libhypre-dev \
    liblapack-dev \
    libblas-dev \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Configure passwordless SSH for root user, a common requirement for MPI runners like mpirun.
# This allows the MPI master process to SSH into other containers (pods) to start worker processes.
RUN mkdir -p /root/.ssh && \
    ssh-keygen -t rsa -f /root/.ssh/id_rsa -N '' && \
    cat /root/.ssh/id_rsa.pub >> /root/.ssh/authorized_keys && \
    chmod 600 /root/.ssh/authorized_keys && \
    # Configure sshd to allow root login and disable password authentication
    sed -i 's/#PermitRootLogin prohibit-password/PermitRootLogin yes/' /etc/ssh/sshd_config && \
    sed -i 's/#PasswordAuthentication yes/PasswordAuthentication no/' /etc/ssh/sshd_config && \
    # Add host keys for sshd
    ssh-keygen -A

# Set the working directory for the build process
WORKDIR /opt/build

# Clone the latest versions of MFEM and Laghos from their repositories
RUN git clone https://github.com/mfem/mfem.git && \
    git clone https://github.com/CEED/Laghos.git

# Build the parallel version of MFEM with MPI, Metis, and HYPRE support.
# CORRECTED: Set HYPRE_DIR=/usr to point to the system-installed HYPRE library.
# This ensures the build system uses the correct paths and respects the HYPRE_VERSION
# variable, which is necessary to bypass version auto-detection that fails with
# the libhypre-dev package from Ubuntu.
RUN cd mfem && \
    make parallel -j$(nproc) \
    CXX=mpicxx \
    MFEM_USE_MPI=yes \
    MFEM_USE_METIS_5=yes \
    MFEM_USE_HYPRE=yes \
    HYPRE_DIR=/usr \
    HYPRE_VERSION=22300

# Build the parallel version of Laghos (p-laghos)
# The MFEM_DIR variable is explicitly set to point to the sibling mfem directory.
RUN cd Laghos && \
    make p-laghos -j$(nproc) MFEM_DIR=../mfem

# Copy the compiled Laghos parallel executable to a system path for easy access
# Renaming to 'laghos' for convenience.
RUN cp /opt/build/Laghos/p-laghos /usr/local/bin/laghos

# Create a final application directory and copy the Laghos data files into it
RUN mkdir -p /app && cp /opt/build/Laghos/data/* /app/

# Clean up the build directory to reduce final image size
RUN rm -rf /opt/build

# Set the final working directory to where the application data is located
WORKDIR /app

# Set a default command to start a shell, allowing for interactive use or easy command overrides
CMD ["/bin/bash"]
```

An expert review of the build process and error log has been completed.

### Error Identification

The build is failing during the compilation of the MFEM library, a dependency for Laghos. The specific error is:
```
get_hypre_version.cpp:12:10: fatal error: HYPRE_config.h: No such file or directory
```
This occurs because the MFEM build system is attempting to compile a helper utility to detect the version of the HYPRE library. This process requires the `HYPRE_config.h` header file, which is not included in the `libhypre-dev` package provided by Ubuntu 22.04.

### Root Cause Analysis

The Dockerfile attempts to work around this issue by providing the `HYPRE_VERSION=22300` variable to the `make` command. This variable is intended to bypass the version detection step entirely. However, the build still attempts to compile the helper utility, indicating that the `HYPRE_VERSION` variable is not being respected by the build script in this context.

The root cause is that the MFEM makefile, when the `HYPRE_DIR` variable is not set, defaults to assuming that HYPRE is located in a sibling source directory (e.g., `../hypre`). This "local source" mode causes it to ignore the `HYPRE_VERSION` override and attempt to build the version detection utility using incorrect paths, which ultimately fails.

### Recommended Solution

To resolve this, you must explicitly inform the MFEM build system that you are using a system-installed version of HYPRE. This is done by setting the `HYPRE_DIR` variable to the system's prefix, which is `/usr`. This change ensures the build system uses the correct paths for headers and libraries and correctly respects the `HYPRE_VERSION` variable to bypass the problematic auto-detection step.

The redundant `HYPRE_INCLUDE` and `HYPRE_LIBS` variables can be removed, as setting `HYPRE_DIR` allows the makefile to correctly infer these paths.

Here is the corrected Dockerfile:

# This allows the MPI master process to SSH into other containers (pods) to start worker processes.
RUN mkdir -p /root/.ssh && \
    ssh-keygen -t rsa -f /root/.ssh/id_rsa -N '' && \
    cat /root/.ssh/id_rsa.pub >> /root/.ssh/authorized_keys && \
    chmod 600 /root/.ssh/authorized_keys && \
    # Configure sshd to allow root login and disable password authentication
    sed -i 's/#PermitRootLogin prohibit-password/PermitRootLogin yes/' /etc/ssh/sshd_config && \
    sed -i 's/#PasswordAuthentication yes/PasswordAuthentication no/' /etc/ssh/sshd_config && \
    # Add host keys for sshd
    ssh-keygen -A

WORKDIR /opt/build

RUN git clone https://github.com/mfem/mfem.git && \
    git clone https://github.com/CEED/Laghos.git

# Build the parallel version of MFEM with MPI, Metis, and HYPRE support.

### Error Analysis

The build process for `mfem` is failing because it cannot find the header file `HYPRE_config.h`. The log shows:

```
get_hypre_version.cpp:12:10: fatal error: HYPRE_config.h: No such file or directory

# Base image: Ubuntu 22.04 LTS for a stable, modern environment
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Set non-interactive frontend for package installations
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Install dependencies for building Laghos and its dependencies (MFEM, MPI)
# Includes build tools, compilers, Git, MPI libraries, and other required scientific libraries.
# Also includes OpenSSH for MPI communication across nodes and ca-certificates for network access.
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y \
    build-essential \
    g++ \
    gfortran \
    make \
    git \
    ca-certificates \
    libopenmpi-dev \
    openmpi-bin \
    openssh-client \
    openssh-server \
    libmetis-dev \
    libhypre-dev \
    liblapack-dev \
    libblas-dev \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Configure passwordless SSH for root user, a common requirement for MPI runners like mpirun.
# This allows the MPI master process to SSH into other containers (pods) to start worker processes.
RUN mkdir -p /root/.ssh && \
    ssh-keygen -t rsa -f /root/.ssh/id_rsa -N '' && \
    cat /root/.ssh/id_rsa.pub >> /root/.ssh/authorized_keys && \
    chmod 600 /root/.ssh/authorized_keys && \
    # Configure sshd to allow root login and disable password authentication
    sed -i 's/#PermitRootLogin prohibit-password/PermitRootLogin yes/' /etc/ssh/sshd_config && \
    sed -i 's/#PasswordAuthentication yes/PasswordAuthentication no/' /etc/ssh/sshd_config && \
    # Add host keys for sshd
    ssh-keygen -A

# Set the working directory for the build process
WORKDIR /opt/build

# Clone the latest versions of MFEM and Laghos from their repositories
RUN git clone https://github.com/mfem/mfem.git && \
    git clone https://github.com/CEED/Laghos.git

# We explicitly set HYPRE_VERSION to bypass MFEM's version detection,
# which fails because the system's libhypre-dev package on Ubuntu 22.04 lacks HYPRE_config.h.
# The version 22300 corresponds to HYPRE 2.23.0.
# The HYPRE_INCLUDE path must point to /usr/include, where headers are installed.
RUN cd mfem && \
    make parallel -j$(nproc) \
    CXX=mpicxx \
    MFEM_USE_MPI=yes \
    MFEM_USE_METIS_5=yes \
    MFEM_USE_HYPRE=yes \
    HYPRE_INCLUDE=-I/usr/include \
    HYPRE_LIBS=-lHYPRE \
    HYPRE_VERSION=22300

# Build the parallel version of Laghos (p-laghos)
# The MFEM_DIR variable is explicitly set to point to the sibling mfem directory.
RUN cd Laghos && \
    make p-laghos -j$(nproc) MFEM_DIR=../mfem

# Copy the compiled Laghos parallel executable to a system path for easy access
# Renaming to 'laghos' for convenience.
RUN cp /opt/build/Laghos/p-laghos /usr/local/bin/laghos

# Create a final application directory and copy the Laghos data files into it
RUN mkdir -p /app && cp /opt/build/Laghos/data/* /app/

# Clean up the build directory to reduce final image size
RUN rm -rf /opt/build

# Set the final working directory to where the application data is located
WORKDIR /app

# Set a default command to start a shell, allowing for interactive use or easy command overrides
CMD ["/bin/bash"]

The build is failing during the compilation of the MFEM library, a dependency for Laghos. The specific error is:
```

```
This occurs because the MFEM build system is attempting to compile a helper utility to detect the version of the HYPRE library. This process requires the `HYPRE_config.h` header file, which is not included in the `libhypre-dev` package provided by Ubuntu 22.04.

The Dockerfile attempts to work around this issue by providing the `HYPRE_VERSION=22300` variable to the `make` command. This variable is intended to bypass the version detection step entirely. The root cause is that the MFEM makefile, when the `HYPRE_DIR` variable is not set, defaults to assuming that HYPRE is located in a sibling source directory (e.g., `../hypre`). The attempt in the original Dockerfile to manually specify the HYPRE version (`HYPRE_VERSION=22300`) to bypass this check was not effective, as the build process still tried to compile the helper program.

### Recommended Solution

The most robust solution is to avoid using the system-provided `libhypre-dev` package altogether and instead leverage MFEM's built-in capability to manage its own dependencies. The MFEM makefile is designed to automatically download, configure, and build a compatible version of HYPRE if one is not explicitly provided.

This requires two modifications to the Dockerfile:

1.  Remove `libhypre-dev` from the list of packages installed by `apt-get`.
2.  Remove the `HYPRE_INCLUDE`, `HYPRE_LIBS`, and `HYPRE_VERSION` flags from the MFEM `make` command.

This ensures that MFEM is built against a known-compatible version of HYPRE that is correctly configured for a parallel MPI environment, resolving the build error and improving the reliability of the build process.

Please find the corrected Dockerfile below.

```dockerfile
# Base image: Ubuntu 22.04 LTS for a stable, modern environment
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Set non-interactive frontend for package installations
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Install dependencies for building Laghos and its dependencies (MFEM, MPI)
# Includes build tools, compilers, Git, MPI libraries, and other required scientific libraries.
# Also includes OpenSSH for MPI communication across nodes and ca-certificates for network access.
# libhypre-dev is removed as we will let MFEM build its own version of HYPRE to ensure compatibility.
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y \
    build-essential \
    g++ \
    gfortran \
    make \
    git \
    ca-certificates \
    libopenmpi-dev \
    openmpi-bin \
    openssh-client \
    openssh-server \
    libmetis-dev \
    liblapack-dev \
    libblas-dev \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Configure passwordless SSH for root user, a common requirement for MPI runners like mpirun.
# This allows the MPI master process to SSH into other containers (pods) to start worker processes.
RUN mkdir -p /root/.ssh && \
    ssh-keygen -t rsa -f /root/.ssh/id_rsa -N '' && \
    cat /root/.ssh/id_rsa.pub >> /root/.ssh/authorized_keys && \
    chmod 600 /root/.ssh/authorized_keys && \
    # Configure sshd to allow root login and disable password authentication
    sed -i 's/#PermitRootLogin prohibit-password/PermitRootLogin yes/' /etc/ssh/sshd_config && \
    sed -i 's/#PasswordAuthentication yes/PasswordAuthentication no/' /etc/ssh/sshd_config && \
    # Add host keys for sshd
    ssh-keygen -A

# Set the working directory for the build process
WORKDIR /opt/build

# Clone the latest versions of MFEM and Laghos from their repositories
RUN git clone https://github.com/mfem/mfem.git && \
    git clone https://github.com/CEED/Laghos.git

# Build the parallel version of MFEM with MPI, Metis, and HYPRE support.
# We let the MFEM build system download and build its own internal version of HYPRE.
# This avoids issues with the system's libhypre-dev package on Ubuntu 22.04,
# which is missing the HYPRE_config.h header file required by MFEM's build process.
RUN cd mfem && \
    make parallel -j$(nproc) \
    CXX=mpicxx \
    MFEM_USE_MPI=yes \
    MFEM_USE_METIS_5=yes \
    MFEM_USE_HYPRE=yes

# Build the parallel version of Laghos (p-laghos)
# The MFEM_DIR variable is explicitly set to point to the sibling mfem directory.
RUN cd Laghos && \
    make p-laghos -j$(nproc) MFEM_DIR=../mfem

# Copy the compiled Laghos parallel executable to a system path for easy access
# Renaming to 'laghos' for convenience.
RUN cp /opt/build/Laghos/p-laghos /usr/local/bin/laghos

# Create a final application directory and copy the Laghos data files into it
RUN mkdir -p /app && cp /opt/build/Laghos/data/* /app/

# Clean up the build directory to reduce final image size
RUN rm -rf /opt/build

# Set the final working directory to where the application data is located
WORKDIR /app

# Set a default command to start a shell, allowing for interactive use or easy command overrides
CMD ["/bin/bash"]

An expert review of the build process and error log has been completed.

### Error Identification

The build is failing during the compilation of the MFEM library, a dependency for Laghos. The specific error is:
```
get_hypre_version.cpp:12:10: fatal error: HYPRE_config.h: No such file or directory
```
This occurs because the MFEM build system is attempting to compile a helper utility to detect the version of the HYPRE library. This process requires the `HYPRE_config.h` header file, which is not included in the `libhypre-dev` package provided by Ubuntu 22.04.

### Root Cause Analysis

The Dockerfile attempts to work around this issue by providing the `HYPRE_VERSION=22300` variable to the `make` command. This variable is intended to bypass the version detection step entirely. However, the build still attempts to compile the helper utility, indicating that the `HYPRE_VERSION` variable is not being respected by the build script in this context.

The root cause is that the MFEM makefile, when the `HYPRE_DIR` variable is not set, defaults to assuming that HYPRE is located in a sibling source directory (e.g., `../hypre`). This "local source" mode causes it to ignore the `HYPRE_VERSION` override and attempt to build the version detection utility using incorrect paths, which ultimately fails.

### Recommended Solution

To resolve this, you must explicitly inform the MFEM build system that you are using a system-installed version of HYPRE. This is done by setting the `HYPRE_DIR` variable to the system's prefix, which is `/usr`. This change ensures the build system uses the correct paths for headers and libraries and correctly respects the `HYPRE_VERSION` variable to bypass the problematic auto-detection step.

The redundant `HYPRE_INCLUDE` and `HYPRE_LIBS` variables can be removed, as setting `HYPRE_DIR` allows the makefile to correctly infer these paths.

# This allows the MPI master process to SSH into other containers (pods) to start worker processes.
RUN mkdir -p /root/.ssh && \
    ssh-keygen -t rsa -f /root/.ssh/id_rsa -N '' && \
    cat /root/.ssh/id_rsa.pub >> /root/.ssh/authorized_keys && \
    chmod 600 /root/.ssh/authorized_keys && \
    # Configure sshd to allow root login and disable password authentication
    sed -i 's/#PermitRootLogin prohibit-password/PermitRootLogin yes/' /etc/ssh/sshd_config && \
    sed -i 's/#PasswordAuthentication yes/PasswordAuthentication no/' /etc/ssh/sshd_config && \
    # Add host keys for sshd

An expert debugging agent has analyzed the issue.

### Error Identification

The build is failing during the compilation of MFEM, a dependency of Laghos. The specific error is:
```
fatal error: HYPRE_config.h: No such file or directory
```
This occurs because the MFEM build system is trying to automatically detect the version of the installed HYPRE library by compiling a helper program. However, the `libhypre-dev` package on Ubuntu 22.04 does not provide the `HYPRE_config.h` header file, causing the compilation of this helper program to fail.

The Dockerfile author correctly identified this potential issue and attempted to bypass the auto-detection by providing the version manually with `HYPRE_VERSION=22300`. Unfortunately, due to the order in which GNU Make expands variables and executes shell commands within the makefile, this command-line variable is not being recognized in time to prevent the faulty auto-detection step from running.

### Recommended Solution

To resolve this, we will modify the `make` command to set `HYPRE_VERSION` as an environment variable for the command's execution context. This ensures the variable is available to the make process and its sub-processes before the auto-detection logic is evaluated.

Please apply the following change to the Dockerfile:

**Original Code Block:**
```dockerfile
RUN cd mfem && \
    make parallel -j$(nproc) \
    CXX=mpicxx \
    MFEM_USE_MPI=yes \
    MFEM_USE_METIS_5=yes \
    MFEM_USE_HYPRE=yes \
    HYPRE_INCLUDE=-I/usr/include \
    HYPRE_LIBS=-lHYPRE \
    HYPRE_VERSION=22300
```

**Corrected Code Block:**
```dockerfile
RUN cd mfem && \
    HYPRE_VERSION=22300 make parallel -j$(nproc) \
    CXX=mpicxx \
    MFEM_USE_MPI=yes \
    MFEM_USE_METIS_5=yes \
    MFEM_USE_HYPRE=yes \
    HYPRE_INCLUDE=-I/usr/include \
    HYPRE_LIBS=-lHYPRE
```

This single change moves `HYPRE_VERSION=22300` from an argument to the `make` command to an environment variable declaration preceding it, which will allow the build to complete successfully.

An expert review of the build process and error log has been completed.

### Error Identification

The build is failing during the compilation of the MFEM library, a dependency for Laghos. The specific error is:
```
get_hypre_version.cpp:12:10: fatal error: HYPRE_config.h: No such file or directory
```
This occurs because the MFEM build system is attempting to compile a helper utility to detect the version of the HYPRE library. This process requires the `HYPRE_config.h` header file, which is not included in the `libhypre-dev` package provided by Ubuntu 22.04.

### Root Cause Analysis

The Dockerfile attempts to work around this issue by providing the `HYPRE_VERSION=22300` variable to the `make` command. This variable is intended to bypass the version detection step entirely. However, the build still attempts to compile the helper utility, indicating that the `HYPRE_VERSION` variable is not being respected by the build script in this context.

The root cause is that the MFEM makefile, when the `HYPRE_DIR` variable is not set, defaults to assuming that HYPRE is located in a sibling source directory (e.g., `../hypre`). This "local source" mode causes it to ignore the `HYPRE_VERSION` override and attempt to build the version detection utility using incorrect paths, which ultimately fails.

### Recommended Solution

To resolve this, you must explicitly inform the MFEM build system that you are using a system-installed version of HYPRE. This is done by setting the `HYPRE_DIR` variable to the system's prefix, which is `/usr`. This change ensures the build system uses the correct paths for headers and libraries and correctly respects the `HYPRE_VERSION` variable to bypass the problematic auto-detection step.

The redundant `HYPRE_INCLUDE` and `HYPRE_LIBS` variables can be removed, as setting `HYPRE_DIR` allows the makefile to correctly infer these paths.

Here is the corrected Dockerfile:

FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Set non-interactive frontend for package installations
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Install dependencies for building Laghos and its dependencies (MFEM, MPI)
# Includes build tools, compilers, Git, MPI libraries, and other required scientific libraries.
# Also includes OpenSSH for MPI communication across nodes and ca-certificates for network access.
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y \
    build-essential \
    g++ \
    gfortran \
    make \
    git \
    ca-certificates \
    libopenmpi-dev \
    openmpi-bin \
    openssh-client \
    openssh-server \

# Base image: Ubuntu 22.04 LTS for a stable, modern environment
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Set non-interactive frontend for package installations
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Install dependencies for building Laghos and its dependencies (MFEM, MPI)
# Includes build tools, compilers, Git, MPI libraries, and other required scientific libraries.
# Also includes OpenSSH for MPI communication across nodes and ca-certificates for network access.
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y \
    build-essential \
    g++ \
    gfortran \
    make \
    git \
    ca-certificates \
    libopenmpi-dev \
    openmpi-bin \
    openssh-client \
    openssh-server \
    libmetis-dev \
    libhypre-dev \
    liblapack-dev \
    libblas-dev \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Configure passwordless SSH for root user, a common requirement for MPI runners like mpirun.
# This allows the MPI master process to SSH into other containers (pods) to start worker processes.
RUN mkdir -p /root/.ssh && \
    ssh-keygen -t rsa -f /root/.ssh/id_rsa -N '' && \
    cat /root/.ssh/id_rsa.pub >> /root/.ssh/authorized_keys && \
    chmod 600 /root/.ssh/authorized_keys && \
    # Configure sshd to allow root login and disable password authentication
    sed -i 's/#PermitRootLogin prohibit-password/PermitRootLogin yes/' /etc/ssh/sshd_config && \
    sed -i 's/#PasswordAuthentication yes/PasswordAuthentication no/' /etc/ssh/sshd_config && \
    # Add host keys for sshd
    ssh-keygen -A

# Set the working directory for the build process
WORKDIR /opt/build

# Clone the latest versions of MFEM and Laghos from their repositories
RUN git clone https://github.com/mfem/mfem.git && \
    git clone https://github.com/CEED/Laghos.git

# Build the parallel version of MFEM with MPI, Metis, and HYPRE support.
# We explicitly set HYPRE_VERSION to bypass MFEM's version detection,
# which fails because the system's libhypre-dev package on Ubuntu 22.04 lacks HYPRE_config.h.
# The version 22300 corresponds to HYPRE 2.23.0.
# The HYPRE_INCLUDE path must point to /usr/include, where headers are installed.
RUN cd mfem && \
    make parallel -j$(nproc) \
    CXX=mpicxx \
    MFEM_USE_MPI=yes \
    MFEM_USE_METIS_5=yes \
    MFEM_USE_HYPRE=yes \
    HYPRE_INCLUDE=-I/usr/include \
    HYPRE_LIBS=-lHYPRE \
    HYPRE_VERSION=22300

# Build the parallel version of Laghos (p-laghos)
# The MFEM_DIR variable is explicitly set to point to the sibling mfem directory.
RUN cd Laghos && \
    make p-laghos -j$(nproc) MFEM_DIR=../mfem

# Copy the compiled Laghos parallel executable to a system path for easy access
# Renaming to 'laghos' for convenience.
RUN cp /opt/build/Laghos/p-laghos /usr/local/bin/laghos

# Create a final application directory and copy the Laghos data files into it
RUN mkdir -p /app && cp /opt/build/Laghos/data/* /app/

# Clean up the build directory to reduce final image size
RUN rm -rf /opt/build

# Set the final working directory to where the application data is located
WORKDIR /app

# Set a default command to start a shell, allowing for interactive use or easy command overrides
CMD ["/bin/bash"]

An expert review of the build process and error log has been completed.

### Error Identification

The build is failing during the compilation of the MFEM library, a dependency for Laghos. The specific error is:
```
get_hypre_version.cpp:12:10: fatal error: HYPRE_config.h: No such file or directory
```
This occurs because the MFEM build system is attempting to compile a helper utility to detect the version of the HYPRE library. This process requires the `HYPRE_config.h` header file, which is not included in the `libhypre-dev` package provided by Ubuntu 22.04.

### Root Cause Analysis

The Dockerfile attempts to work around this issue by providing the `HYPRE_VERSION=22300` variable to the `make` command. This variable is intended to bypass the version detection step entirely. However, the build still attempts to compile the helper utility, indicating that the `HYPRE_VERSION` variable is not being respected by the build script in this context.

The root cause is that the MFEM makefile, when the `HYPRE_DIR` variable is not set, defaults to assuming that HYPRE is located in a sibling source directory (e.g., `../hypre`). This "local source" mode causes it to ignore the `HYPRE_VERSION` override and attempt to build the version detection utility using incorrect paths, which ultimately fails.

### Recommended Solution

To resolve this, you must explicitly inform the MFEM build system that you are using a system-installed version of HYPRE. This is done by setting the `HYPRE_DIR` variable to the system's prefix, which is `/usr`. This change ensures the build system uses the correct paths for headers and libraries and correctly respects the `HYPRE_VERSION` variable to bypass the problematic auto-detection step.

The redundant `HYPRE_INCLUDE` and `HYPRE_LIBS` variables can be removed, as setting `HYPRE_DIR` allows the makefile to correctly infer these paths.

This is a known issue with the `libhypre-dev` package on Ubuntu 22.04, which does not include `HYPRE_config.h`. The Dockerfile attempts to work around this by providing the `HYPRE_VERSION` variable directly to `make`. However, the build system is still getting confused about where to find the HYPRE library, as indicated by its attempt to use a relative include path (`-I../../hypre/src/hypre/include`) instead of the system path (`/usr/include`). This happens because the MFEM makefile system was not explicitly told to use the system-wide installation path for HYPRE.

To resolve this, we must explicitly point the MFEM build system to the system's library installation directory (`/usr`). This is done by replacing the `HYPRE_INCLUDE` and `HYPRE_LIBS` variables with `HYPRE_DIR=/usr`. The `HYPRE_VERSION` variable is still required to bypass the script that searches for the missing header file.

# Base image: Ubuntu 22.04 LTS for a stable, modern environment
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Set non-interactive frontend for package installations
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Install dependencies for building Laghos and its dependencies (MFEM, MPI)
# Includes build tools, compilers, Git, MPI libraries, and other required scientific libraries.
# Also includes OpenSSH for MPI communication across nodes and ca-certificates for network access.
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y \
    build-essential \
    g++ \
    gfortran \
    make \
    git \
    ca-certificates \
    libopenmpi-dev \
    openmpi-bin \
    openssh-client \
    openssh-server \
    libmetis-dev \
    libhypre-dev \
    liblapack-dev \
    libblas-dev \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Configure passwordless SSH for root user, a common requirement for MPI runners like mpirun.
# This allows the MPI master process to SSH into other containers (pods) to start worker processes.
RUN mkdir -p /root/.ssh && \
    ssh-keygen -t rsa -f /root/.ssh/id_rsa -N '' && \
    cat /root/.ssh/id_rsa.pub >> /root/.ssh/authorized_keys && \
    chmod 600 /root/.ssh/authorized_keys && \
    # Configure sshd to allow root login and disable password authentication
    sed -i 's/#PermitRootLogin prohibit-password/PermitRootLogin yes/' /etc/ssh/sshd_config && \
    sed -i 's/#PasswordAuthentication yes/PasswordAuthentication no/' /etc/ssh/sshd_config && \
    # Add host keys for sshd
    ssh-keygen -A

# Set the working directory for the build process
WORKDIR /opt/build

# Clone the latest versions of MFEM and Laghos from their repositories
RUN git clone https://github.com/mfem/mfem.git && \
    git clone https://github.com/CEED/Laghos.git

# Build the parallel version of MFEM with MPI, Metis, and HYPRE support.
# We explicitly set HYPRE_VERSION to bypass MFEM's version detection,
# which fails because the system's libhypre-dev package on Ubuntu 22.04 lacks HYPRE_config.h.
# The version 22300 corresponds to HYPRE 2.23.0.
# The HYPRE_INCLUDE path must point to /usr/include, where headers are installed.
RUN cd mfem && \
    make parallel -j$(nproc) \
    CXX=mpicxx \
    MFEM_USE_MPI=yes \
    MFEM_USE_METIS_5=yes \
    MFEM_USE_HYPRE=yes \
    HYPRE_INCLUDE=-I/usr/include \
    HYPRE_LIBS=-lHYPRE \
    HYPRE_VERSION=22300

# Build the parallel version of Laghos (p-laghos)
# The MFEM_DIR variable is explicitly set to point to the sibling mfem directory.
RUN cd Laghos && \
    make p-laghos -j$(nproc) MFEM_DIR=../mfem

# Copy the compiled Laghos parallel executable to a system path for easy access
# Renaming to 'laghos' for convenience.
RUN cp /opt/build/Laghos/p-laghos /usr/local/bin/laghos

# Create a final application directory and copy the Laghos data files into it
RUN mkdir -p /app && cp /opt/build/Laghos/data/* /app/

# Clean up the build directory to reduce final image size
RUN rm -rf /opt/build

# Set the final working directory to where the application data is located
WORKDIR /app

# Set a default command to start a shell, allowing for interactive use or easy command overrides
CMD ["/bin/bash"]

An expert review of the build process and error log has been completed.

### Error Identification

The build is failing during the compilation of the MFEM library, a dependency for Laghos. The specific error is:
```
get_hypre_version.cpp:12:10: fatal error: HYPRE_config.h: No such file or directory
```
This occurs because the MFEM build system is attempting to compile a helper utility to detect the version of the HYPRE library. This process requires the `HYPRE_config.h` header file, which is not included in the `libhypre-dev` package provided by Ubuntu 22.04.

### Root Cause Analysis

The Dockerfile attempts to work around this issue by providing the `HYPRE_VERSION=22300` variable to the `make` command. This variable is intended to bypass the version detection step entirely. However, the build still attempts to compile the helper utility, indicating that the `HYPRE_VERSION` variable is not being respected by the build script in this context.

The root cause is that the MFEM makefile, when the `HYPRE_DIR` variable is not set, defaults to assuming that HYPRE is located in a sibling source directory (e.g., `../hypre`). This "local source" mode causes it to ignore the `HYPRE_VERSION` override and attempt to build the version detection utility using incorrect paths, which ultimately fails.

### Recommended Solution

To resolve this, you must explicitly inform the MFEM build system that you are using a system-installed version of HYPRE. This is done by setting the `HYPRE_DIR` variable to the system's prefix, which is `/usr`. This change ensures the build system uses the correct paths for headers and libraries and correctly respects the `HYPRE_VERSION` variable to bypass the problematic auto-detection step.

The redundant `HYPRE_INCLUDE` and `HYPRE_LIBS` variables can be removed, as setting `HYPRE_DIR` allows the makefile to correctly infer these paths.

An expert review of the build process and error log has been completed.

### Error Identification

The build is failing during the compilation of the MFEM library, a dependency for Laghos. The specific error is:
```
get_hypre_version.cpp:12:10: fatal error: HYPRE_config.h: No such file or directory
```
This occurs because the MFEM build system is attempting to compile a helper utility to detect the version of the HYPRE library. This process requires the `HYPRE_config.h` header file, which is not included in the `libhypre-dev` package provided by Ubuntu 22.04.

### Root Cause Analysis

The Dockerfile attempts to work around this issue by providing the `HYPRE_VERSION=22300` variable to the `make` command. This variable is intended to bypass the version detection step entirely. However, the build still attempts to compile the helper utility, indicating that the `HYPRE_VERSION` variable is not being respected by the build script in this context.

The root cause is that the MFEM makefile, when the `HYPRE_DIR` variable is not set, defaults to assuming that HYPRE is located in a sibling source directory (e.g., `../hypre`). This "local source" mode causes it to ignore the `HYPRE_VERSION` override and attempt to build the version detection utility using incorrect paths, which ultimately fails.

### Recommended Solution

To resolve this, you must explicitly inform the MFEM build system that you are using a system-installed version of HYPRE. This is done by setting the `HYPRE_DIR` variable to the system's prefix, which is `/usr`. This change ensures the build system uses the correct paths for headers and libraries and correctly respects the `HYPRE_VERSION` variable to bypass the problematic auto-detection step.

The redundant `HYPRE_INCLUDE` and `HYPRE_LIBS` variables can be removed, as setting `HYPRE_DIR` allows the makefile to correctly infer these paths.

An expert review of the build process and error log has been completed.

### Error Identification

The build is failing during the compilation of the MFEM library, a dependency for Laghos. The specific error is:
```
get_hypre_version.cpp:12:10: fatal error: HYPRE_config.h: No such file or directory
```
This occurs because the MFEM build system is attempting to compile a helper utility to detect the version of the HYPRE library. This process requires the `HYPRE_config.h` header file, which is not included in the `libhypre-dev` package provided by Ubuntu 22.04.

### Root Cause Analysis

The Dockerfile attempts to work around this issue by providing the `HYPRE_VERSION=22300` variable to the `make` command. This variable is intended to bypass the version detection step entirely. However, the build still attempts to compile the helper utility, indicating that the `HYPRE_VERSION` variable is not being respected by the build script in this context.

The root cause is that the MFEM makefile, when the `HYPRE_DIR` variable is not set, defaults to assuming that HYPRE is located in a sibling source directory (e.g., `../hypre`). This "local source" mode causes it to ignore the `HYPRE_VERSION` override and attempt to build the version detection utility using incorrect paths, which ultimately fails.

### Recommended Solution

To resolve this, you must explicitly inform the MFEM build system that you are using a system-installed version of HYPRE. This is done by setting the `HYPRE_DIR` variable to the system's prefix, which is `/usr`. This change ensures the build system uses the correct paths for headers and libraries and correctly respects the `HYPRE_VERSION` variable to bypass the problematic auto-detection step.

The redundant `HYPRE_INCLUDE` and `HYPRE_LIBS` variables can be removed, as setting `HYPRE_DIR` allows the makefile to correctly infer these paths.

dockerfile.item:
# Base image: Ubuntu 22.04 LTS for a stable, modern environment
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Set non-interactive frontend for package installations
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Install dependencies for building Laghos and its dependencies (MFEM, MPI)
# Includes build tools, compilers, Git, MPI libraries, and other required scientific libraries.
# Also includes OpenSSH for MPI communication across nodes and ca-certificates for network access.
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y \
    build-essential \
    g++ \
    gfortran \
    make \
    git \
    ca-certificates \
    libopenmpi-dev \
    openmpi-bin \
    openssh-client \
    openssh-server \
    libmetis-dev \
    libhypre-dev \
    liblapack-dev \
    libblas-dev \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Configure passwordless SSH for root user, a common requirement for MPI runners like mpirun.
# This allows the MPI master process to SSH into other containers (pods) to start worker processes.
RUN mkdir -p /root/.ssh && \
    ssh-keygen -t rsa -f /root/.ssh/id_rsa -N '' && \
    cat /root/.ssh/id_rsa.pub >> /root/.ssh/authorized_keys && \
    chmod 600 /root/.ssh/authorized_keys && \
    # Configure sshd to allow root login and disable password authentication
    sed -i 's/#PermitRootLogin prohibit-password/PermitRootLogin yes/' /etc/ssh/sshd_config && \
    sed -i 's/#PasswordAuthentication yes/PasswordAuthentication no/' /etc/ssh/sshd_config && \
    # Add host keys for sshd
    ssh-keygen -A

# Set the working directory for the build process
WORKDIR /opt/build

# Clone the latest versions of MFEM and Laghos from their repositories
RUN git clone https://github.com/mfem/mfem.git && \
    git clone https://github.com/CEED/Laghos.git

# Build the parallel version of MFEM with MPI, Metis, and HYPRE support.
# We explicitly set HYPRE_VERSION to bypass MFEM's version detection,
# which fails because the system's libhypre-dev package on Ubuntu 22.04 lacks HYPRE_config.h.
# The version 22300 corresponds to HYPRE 2.23.0.
# The HYPRE_INCLUDE path must point to /usr/include, where headers are installed.
RUN cd mfem && \
    make parallel -j$(nproc) \
    CXX=mpicxx \
    MFEM_USE_MPI=yes \
    MFEM_USE_METIS_5=yes \
    MFEM_USE_HYPRE=yes \
    HYPRE_INCLUDE=-I/usr/include \
    HYPRE_LIBS=-lHYPRE \
    HYPRE_VERSION=22300

# Build the parallel version of Laghos (p-laghos)
# The MFEM_DIR variable is explicitly set to point to the sibling mfem directory.
RUN cd Laghos && \
    make p-laghos -j$(nproc) MFEM_DIR=../mfem

# Copy the compiled Laghos parallel executable to a system path for easy access
# Renaming to 'laghos' for convenience.
RUN cp /opt/build/Laghos/p-laghos /usr/local/bin/laghos

# Create a final application directory and copy the Laghos data files into it
RUN mkdir -p /app && cp /opt/build/Laghos/data/* /app/

# Clean up the build directory to reduce final image size
RUN rm -rf /opt/build

# Set the final working directory to where the application data is located
WORKDIR /app

# Set a default command to start a shell, allowing for interactive use or easy command overrides
CMD ["/bin/bash"]
